question: Who among the following nationalist leaders was the founder and editor of the Marathi newspaper 'Kesari'?
solution:
The correct answer is** **__**Bal Gangadhar Tilak**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Bal Gangadhar Tilak was the founder and editor of the Marathi newspaper Kesari**

 
 
• **Kesari** is a **Marathi newspaper** that was founded on 4 January 1881** by Lokmanya Bal Gangadhar Tilak**, a prominent leader of the Indian Independence movement.
 
• The newspaper was used as a spokes piece for the Indian national freedom movement and continues to be published by the **Kesari Maratha Trust and Tilak's descendants.**
 
• Bal Gangadhar Tilak used to run his two newspapers, **Kesari, in Marathi and Mahratta in English from Kesari Wada, Narayan Peth, Pune**.
 
• The newspapers were originally started as a co-operative by Chiplunkar, Agarkar, and Tilak. 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The first English Newspaper was started by Irishman James Augustus Hicky in 1779.

 
 
• It was founded in Calcutta.
 
• The name of the First English Newspaper is Hicky's Bengal Gazette.
 
 
 
• In 1811 started ‘Calcutta Chronicle’ and the editor was James Silk Buckingham.
 
 
• He had introduced a new approach to Journalism in India.
 
• He initiated clear journalistic practices and covered the problems of local people and their lives.
 
 
 
• "The Hindu" was started in the English language in 1878, which was mainly distributed in Tamil Nadu and Kerala.
 
• News agency services became available on a regular basis with the Press Trust of India which was started in 1946.
 
• Raja Ram Mohan Roy a social reformer recognized the power of newspapers and started a Bengali newspaper ‘Sambad Kaumudi’ in 1822 and a Persian paper ‘Mirat-ul-Akhbar’ in 1822.
 
• Fardaonji Murzban in 1822 started ‘Bombay Samachar’, he was a pioneer of the Vernacular Press in Bombay.
